extracted.intended_audience: trademark examiners, classification specialists, intellectual property office staff and trademark searchers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal rules for classifying the figurative elements of marks using the Vienna Classification (7th Edition), and related treaty depositary/notification procedures. Covers how to code, where to place elements, formatting of classification codes, and responsibilities for searching and coding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispute settlement (Article 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a dispute between two or more countries of the Special Union concerning interpretation or application of the Agreement is not settled by negotiation, any one of the countries concerned may bring it before the International Court of Justice (ICJ) by application in conformity with the Statute of the Court, unless the parties agree otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The country bringing the dispute must inform the International Bureau; the Bureau shall notify other countries. A country may declare at signature/ratification/accession that it does not consider itself bound by paragraph (1) (the ICJ route); disputes involving a country having made such a declaration are excluded from paragraph (1). Such a declaration may be withdrawn at any time by notification to the Director General.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature, languages, depositary and notification functions (Article 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal treaty provisions on signature, authentic languages, deposit, official texts, transmission of certified copies, registration and notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agreement is signed in single original in English and French (both equally authentic); shall remain open for signature until specified date; original deposited with Director General. Director General may establish official texts in other languages after consultation. Director General shall transmit certified copies of the signed text and of amendments to Governments, furnish certified copies of the Classification on request, register the Agreement with the UN Secretariat, and notify Governments party to the Paris Convention of events including signature, deposits of ratification/accession, entry into force, declarations, withdrawals, acceptances of amendments, dates amendments enter into force, and denunciations (items (i)–(x)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Format of classification numbers (Committee Recommendations)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to write Vienna Classification numbers and the abbreviation to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate category and division, and division and section by a point (e.g., CFE 3.9.10). Separate numbers of different sections with commas (e.g., CFE 3.9.10,24,25). Use a dash to indicate an uninterrupted range of sections (e.g., CFE 3.9.16-18). If section numbers are absent, still separate category and division by a point (e.g., CFE 3.9). If several categories/divisions are necessary for one registration, indicate each separately in numerical order, separated by semicolons (e.g., CFE 1.1.2,10,25; 1.15.17; 2.9.1). Indicate edition by an Arabic numeral in round brackets, e.g., CFE (7). The Committee determined the abbreviation 'CFE' (Classification of Figurative Elements) to precede classification numbers when a country chooses an abbreviation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Classification and required preparatory operations (Guidance for the user)
rubrics_metrics.description: The main purpose of the Classification is to facilitate anticipation searching; effective searching requires two interdependent operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operation (i): consistent and correct classification (coding) of figurative elements in the search file, taking into account future needs of anticipation searching. Operation (ii): correct definition of the sections in which prior marks must be searched, taking into account coding characteristics. Both operations are interdependent and should be entrusted to persons with proven skills in the trademark field, able to assess figurative elements by their distinguishing properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarization and strict use of explanatory material
rubrics_metrics.description: Users must familiarize themselves with certain preparatory materials and abide by Explanatory Notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before using the Classification, users should read the Preface, the Committee's Recommendations and the General Notes. When using the Classification, users should abide strictly by the Explanatory Notes and the references given in them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of the Classification (three headings)
rubrics_metrics.description: How the Classification content is organized for use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Classification is reproduced under three headings: (1) the Table of Categories for rapid guidance, (2) the Table of Categories and Divisions with Explanatory Notes to confine subject matter to appropriate divisions, and (3) the List of Categories, Divisions and Sections with Explanatory Notes to decide final placement. Explanatory notes on a category apply to all its divisions even if not repeated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auxiliary sections notation and code assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: How auxiliary sections are indicated and how they affect coding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections with a letter 'A' before their numerical code are auxiliary sections grouping figurative elements from main sections according to specific criteria. The letter 'A' should not appear in the numerical code assigned to the figurative element at the time of coding (i.e., codes use only the numeric section numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples are informative only
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphic examples included in the manual are not part of the Classification itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examples of figurative elements reproduced (pages indicated) are given for information purposes only and do not form an integral part of the Classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: General placement rules for figurative elements (General Notes a–e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for placing figurative elements in categories, divisions and sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place figurative elements on the basis of shape regardless of material composition or purpose of the object. A representation of an object forming part of another object is classified under the same category/division/section as the object of which it forms part, unless expressly classified elsewhere. If it is not possible to determine clearly which division/section applies, place the element in both divisions/sections (unless a special note says otherwise). Representations similar to those mentioned in a given section are placed in that section even if not expressly listed. If a mark comprises several figurative elements each classified differently, place each element in its appropriate categories/divisions/sections (multiple indications allowed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 1 — Celestial bodies, natural phenomena, geographical maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for stars, comets, sun, earth, moon, constellations, armillary spheres, natural phenomena, geographical maps and related divisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes divisions such as 1.1 (stars, comets), 1.3 (sun) — note: representations of the sun that are solely a disk without rays go to division 26.1; 1.5 (earth, globes, planets), 1.7 (moon, including moon with stars), 1.11 (constellations), 1.13 (armillary spheres, atomic models), 1.15 (natural phenomena — e.g., rainbows, lightning, waves) and 1.17 (geographical maps, planispheres). Notes clarify exclusions (e.g., sparks placed in 1.15.7 or 1.1 exceptions) and auxiliary sections for variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 2 — Human beings
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for representations of human beings and related groupings and body parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 2.1 (men), 2.3 (women), 2.5 (children), 2.7 (mixed groups, scenes), 2.9 (parts of the human body, skeletons, skulls). Notes: inscriptions representing a human being are placed in 27.3.1; heads placed in appropriate sections of divisions 2.1, 2.3, 2.5 or 2.7, not in 2.9.25. Auxiliary sections capture silhouettes, poses, activities, stylized forms, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 3 — Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for animals including various series of quadrupeds, birds, aquatic animals, reptiles, insects, and parts or prehistoric animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include series of quadrupeds (3.1–3.5), parts/skeletons (3.6), birds/bats (3.7), aquatic animals (3.9), reptiles/amphibia (3.11), insects/spiders/micro-organisms (3.13), other animals and prehistoric animals (3.15), and groups of animals classified in different divisions (3.17). Notes: heads of quadrupeds are placed in divisions 3.1–3.5; written/typographical matter representing animals is classified under 27.3.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 4 — Supernatural, fabulous, fantastic or unidentifiable beings
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for winged/horned personages, partly human/partly animal beings, fabulous animals, masks, and groups of figurative elements in this category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 4.1 (winged or horned personages), 4.2 (partly human/animal), 4.3 (fabulous animals), 4.5/4.7 (plants/objects/geometrical figures representing personages or animals; masks or fantastic heads). Note: exclude human beings and fantastic animals composed of letters/figures (these are classified in 27.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 5 — Plants
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for trees, leaves, flowers, grain, vegetables and other plant representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 5.1 (trees, bushes), 5.3 (leaves, needles), 5.5 (flowers, including heraldic flowers), 5.7 (grain, seeds, fruits), 5.9 (vegetables), 5.11 (other plants), 5.13 (decorations made of plants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 6 — Landscapes
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for mountains, water landscapes, deserts, urban landscapes and other landscape types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 6.1 (mountains, rocks), 6.3 (landscapes with water), 6.6 (desert/tropical), 6.7 (urban/village scenes), 6.19 (other landscapes). Notes clarify exclusions (e.g., urban landscapes with water excluded from 6.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 7 — Constructions, structures for advertisements, gates or barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for dwellings, buildings, advertisement hoardings, monuments, structural works, building materials, gates and barriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 7.1 (dwellings, buildings, advertisement hoardings, cages), 7.3 (parts/interiors), 7.5 (monuments, stadiums, fountains), 7.11 (structural works), 7.15 (building materials, walls, gates, scaffolding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 8 — Foodstuffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Category covering baked goods, dairy products, meats, fish and other foodstuffs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 8.1 (bakers' products, pastry, confectionery, chocolate), 8.3 (milk, dairy, cheeses), 8.5 (butchers' meat, pork, fishmongers' products), 8.7 (other foodstuffs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 9 — Textiles, clothing, sewing accessories, headwear, footwear
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for textiles, clothing and related accessories including headwear and footwear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 9.1 (textiles not clothing), 9.3 (clothing — excludes headwear 9.7 and footwear 9.9), 9.5 (sewing accessories, patterns), 9.7 (headwear), 9.9 (footwear).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 10 — Tobacco, smokers' requisites, matches, travel goods, fans, toilet articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Category grouping tobacco-related items, travel goods, fans, bags, toilet articles and mirrors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 10.1 (tobacco, smokers' requisites, matches), 10.3 (travel goods, fans, bags), 10.5 (toilet articles, mirrors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 11 — Household utensils
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for knives, forks, spoons, kitchen utensils and other household utensils (excluding some items classified elsewhere).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 11.1 (knives, forks, spoons, kitchen utensils and machines), 11.3 (containers for beverages, plates and dishes, utensils for serving/preparing/cooking — not including items in 11.1), 11.7 (other household utensils). Note: excludes utensils classified in categories 12, 13 or 19.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 12 — Furniture, sanitary installations
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for furniture (including office furniture) and sanitary installations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 12.1 (furniture) and 12.3 (sanitary installations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 13 — Lighting, wireless valves, heating, cooking or refrigerating equipment, washing/drying equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for lighting, wireless valves and various household/industrial appliances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 13.1 (lighting, wireless valves) and 13.3 (heating, cooking or refrigerating equipment, washing machines, drying equipment). Notes clarify overlaps (e.g., electric lamps in other divisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 14 — Ironmongery, tools, ladders
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for tubes, cables, heavy ironmongery, small ironmongery articles, springs, locks, tools, agricultural implements and ladders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 14.1 (tubes, cables, heavy ironmongery — includes non-metallic ironmongery), 14.3 (small ironmongery, springs), 14.5 (keys, locks, padlocks), 14.7 (tools — including handles), 14.9 (agricultural/horticultural implements), 14.11 (ladders).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 15 — Machinery, motors, engines
rubrics_metrics.description: Category covering industrial machines, household machines, office machines, wheels, bearings and electrical equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 15.1 (machines for industry or agriculture, motors, engines), 15.3 (machines for household use, spinning wheels), 15.5 (office machines), 15.7 (wheels, bearings), 15.9 (electrical equipment). Notes specify exclusions (e.g., electric lamps classified in 13.1.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 16 — Telecommunications, sound recording/reproduction, computers, photography, cinematography, optics
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for telecommunication equipment, audio devices, computers, photographic and cinematographic equipment and optics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 16.1 (telecommunications, sound recording/reproduction, computers) and 16.3 (photography, cinematography, optics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 17 — Horological instruments, jewelry, weights and measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for time-measuring instruments, jewelry, balances, weights and measures; includes calculating instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 17.1 (horological/time instruments), 17.2 (jewelry), 17.3 (balances, weights), 17.5 (measures). Note: includes calculating instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 18 — Transport, equipment for animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for land vehicles, equipment for animals, water/ amphibious vehicles, anchors, buoys, aerial/space vehicles and traffic signs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 18.1 (land vehicles), 18.2 (equipment for animals), 18.3 (vehicles for use on water/amphibious), 18.4 (anchors; buoys or lifebelts), 18.5 (aerial or space vehicles), 18.7 (traffic signs and indicator boards). Notes exclude military tanks/aircraft/warships (classified elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 19 — Containers and packing, representations of miscellaneous products
rubrics_metrics.description: Category covering large and small containers, bottles, amphorae, coffins, lab receptacles, medical apparatus and representations of miscellaneous products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 19.1 (large containers), 19.3 (small containers — excludes items classified in other specific divisions), 19.7 (bottles, flasks), 19.8 (parts/accessories of bottles), 19.9 (amphorae, pitchers, vases), 19.10 (coffins, funerary urns), 19.11 (receptacles for laboratory/pharmacy use), 19.13 (medical or surgical apparatus, prostheses, medicines), 19.19 (representations of miscellaneous products like coal, ingots).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 20 — Writing, drawing or painting materials, office requisites, stationery and booksellers' goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for pens, small office requisites, papers, documents, books and bookbindings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 20.1 (writing, drawing or painting materials, small office requisites), 20.5 (papers, documents), 20.7 (books, bookbindings, newspapers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 21 — Games, toys, sporting articles, roundabouts
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for games, toys and sporting articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 21.1 (games, toys) and 21.3 (sporting articles, roundabouts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 22 — Musical instruments and accessories, bells, pictures, sculptures
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for musical instruments and accessories, bells and visual arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 22.1 (musical instruments and accessories), 22.3 (bells), 22.5 (pictures, sculptures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 23 — Arms, ammunition, armour
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for side arms, firearms, ammunition, explosives and armour, with exclusions for certain military vehicles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 23.1 (side arms, other weapons not firearms), 23.3 (firearms, ammunition, explosives), 23.5 (armour). Note: excludes military tanks (18.1.14), military aircraft (18.5.1) and warships (18.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 24 — Heraldry, coins, emblems, symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for shields, seals, medals, flags, crowns, emblems, crosses, arrows, signs and notations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 24.1 (shields), 24.3 (seals, stamps), 24.5 (medals, coins), 24.7 (flags), 24.9 (crowns, diadems), 24.11 (emblems, insignia), 24.13 (crosses), 24.15 (arrows) and 24.17 (signs, notations, symbols). Notes address inclusions/exclusions (e.g., arrows includes darts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 25 — Ornamental motifs, surfaces or backgrounds with ornaments
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for ornamental motifs, horizontally elongated ornamental surfaces, backgrounds divided into two or four, and surfaces covered with repeated figures or inscriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 25.1 (ornamental motifs), 25.3 (horizontally elongated ornamental surfaces), 25.5 (backgrounds divided into two or four), 25.7 (surfaces/backgrounds covered with repeated geometrical figures/figurative elements/inscriptions), 25.12 (surfaces/backgrounds covered with other ornaments). Notes clarify classification of plant-composed motifs (5.13) and elongated shapes (26.x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 26 — Geometrical figures and solids
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for circles, ellipses, angles, triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, juxtaposed/intersecting figures, lines and bands, indefinable geometrical figures and solids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 26.1 (circles, ellipses), 26.2 (segments/sectors), 26.3 (triangles/angles), 26.4 (quadrilaterals), 26.5 (other polygons), 26.7 (different geometrical figures juxtaposed/joined/intersecting), 26.11 (lines, bands), 26.13 (other geometrical figures, indefinable designs), 26.15 (geometrical solids). Notes: include geometrical figures composed of people/animals/plants/objects; inscriptions forming geometrical figures are classified in 27.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 27 — Forms of writing, numerals
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for letters or numerals forming geometrical figures, letters/numerals representing humans/animals/plants/objects, special forms of writing and numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 27.1 (letters/numerals forming geometrical figures, typographical matter in perspective), 27.3 (letters/numerals representing human/animal/plant/heavenly bodies/objects — includes punctuation marks used similarly), 27.5 (letters presenting a special form of writing — includes single letters or series/words), 27.7 (numerals presenting special form).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 28 — Inscriptions in various characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for inscriptions in different scripts and characters, with the caveat that divisions relating to a country's normal characters may be disregarded (then treated as word marks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions include 28.1 (Arabic characters), 28.3 (Chinese or Japanese characters), 28.5 (Cyrillic), 28.7 (Greek), 28.9 (Hebrew), 28.11 (Latin), 28.17 (historical/cuneiform/hieroglyphic), 28.19 (other characters). Note: in a given country, divisions relating to characters normally used there may not be used for classification (those inscriptions are word marks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 29 — Colours
rubrics_metrics.description: Category for colours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Division 29.1 covers colours (treatment of colours as figurative elements).
